home.seo.what: A retrospective is a recurring team meeting that examines not the work itself but how the team works: what got in the way, what helped, what changes next sprint. Teams run it at the end of a sprint or every two to four weeks, and it should end with a list of actions and owners, not a list of conclusions.
home.seo.h2.why: Why a board and not just a call
home.seo.why: On a call the loudest person speaks and the rest agree. On a board everyone writes at once, in silence — and the half of the team that usually stays quiet finally says something. Voting then filters out the noise, and the discussion goes to whatever actually earned votes. All of it stays in one place until next time.
home.seo.how: A board is one click away and lives behind an unguessable link — no signup, no email, no invitations. Inside: three columns, likes and dislikes, comments, images, a shared timer and a discussion mode that highlights the same card on everyone’s screen. Results export to Markdown or JSON.
home.faq.heading: Common questions
home.faq.a1: Entirely. Boards, spaces, votes, comments, images and export — no plans and no cap on participants. The project is open source, the code is on GitHub.
home.faq.a2: No. You create a board and share the link — everyone joins through it, with no accounts and no email. People set their own name, and even that is optional.
home.faq.q3: How many people can one board hold?
home.faq.a3: There is no participant limit. Updates reach everyone in real time, and the counter in the header shows who is on the board right now.
home.faq.a4: Only the people you gave the link to. Boards are closed to search engines, and card and comment contents are stored encrypted. A space can additionally be locked with a password.
home.faq.a5: Yes — one-click export to Markdown or JSON. There is also an API to fetch a board by URL, which helps when a bot or an AI agent picks up the results.
